children: Commerce Bancshares’ net interest income and earnings rose year over year, as higher loan balances—largely from the FineMark acquisition—lifted interest income. Trust and bank card fees also increased, while a lower credit-loss provision contributed to growth; higher salaries, technology and acquisition-related costs partly offset those gains.
² Reported as “Net income attributable to Commerce Bancshares, Inc.”. ³ Reported as “Net income per common share — diluted”.
: Completed Jan. 1, adding approximately $4.0 billion in assets, $2.6 billion in loans and 13 banking offices.
: Increased 10.5% year over year, mainly on higher loan interest income and securities purchased under resale agreements.
: Rose $15.0 million, or 25.7%, primarily on growth in private client trust fees.
: Third-quarter net loan charge-offs were $10.6 million; annualized net charge-offs were 0.20% of average loans.
